newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-WAUGH IN THE RECORD-BOOKS AS AUSTRALIA PRESS ON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH IN THE RECORD-BOOKS AS AUSTRALIA PRESS ON.

text.p: Steve Waugh went into the record-books with a century in each innings as Australia piled on runs and discomfort in the third test against England on Sunday.
Waugh became the first player for 50 years to score a century in each innings of an Ashes test and only the third Australian to do so.
The last instance was by Australia's Arthur Morris and England's Denis Compton in the high-scoring Adelaide test of 1946-47.
Waugh, suffering from a bruised hand, eventually touched a catch to wicket-keeper Alec Stewart after six hours and 20 minutes at the crease, having scored 116.
At lunch on the fourth day Australia were 367 for eight in their second innings -- a lead of 440, which is more than any team has ever made in the fourth innings to win a test.
With the weather good, they appeared well placed to level the six-match series at one-each, with three to play.

Even Shane Warne, who was expected to be the key bowler when England batted again on a wearing pitch, weighed in with the bat. He made his second-highest test score of 53 before touching Andy Caddick's first ball of the day to Stewart.
Taking the new ball first thing did England no good whatsoever as Waugh and Warne plundered 30 runs off the opening three overs from Dean Headley and Darren Gough.
There was another blow for England when opening batsman Mark Butcher was forced to leave the field after being hit on the hand while fielding.
Small consolations for them were Headley's eight wickets on debut and Stewart's eight catches, an English record in Ashes tests.
Headley was unable to claim his fifth wicket of the innings before lunch as Paul Reiffel (27 not out) and Jason Gillespie ( 18 not out) stretched the lead to formidable proportions.
